title: Duet recipe
description: A recipe's recipe.json: how to make one kind of project on one system. Its folder also holds files/ (the new project's files), instructions.md (added to the agent's system prompt) and skills/ (the agent's skills there), all optional.

title.description: Its name in the list of recipes, e.g. "Qt Widgets · CMake · MSVC".

description.description: Shown under the list when it is chosen: what the new project holds and what it needs.

systems.description: The systems it is made for; every system when it is not given.

language.description: The language family it is attached to in a project; none for a recipe of no language.

environment.description: What it adds to the environment of the project's terminals, run configurations and agent sessions.

visualStudio.description: Windows: the MSVC developer environment, as an x64 Native Tools prompt has it (cl, link, the SDK, Visual Studio's CMake and Ninja).

path.description: Folders put first in the PATH.

requires.description: The tools its projects need: Duet downloads those missing to ~/.duet/tools, and puts them in the project's environment as each one says.

run.description: Written to the new project's .duet/run.json; added to an existing project's own configurations. {{identifier}} in a command or a folder stands for the project's identifier.

setup.description: Commands run once, one after the other, when the new project is first opened (npm install, a CMake configure): what Build needs before it works. {{identifier}} stands for the project's identifier.

prompts.description: Prompts typed in the agent's prompt from the Project menu, for the user to complete.

title.description: Its name in the Project menu.

text.description: The text typed in the agent's prompt.

parameters.description: Choices the new project is made with, offered when it is created and kept in the project. {{name}} stands for the value chosen, and the value's variables for theirs, in the recipe's files, requirements, commands, prompts, instructions and servers.

title.description: Its label in the New Project form; the name when it is not given.

values.description: The values offered, the first one by default: a value, or a value with the placeholders it sets.

variables.description: Placeholders set with the value, e.g. {"typescript": "~6.0.0"} for {{typescript}}.

languageServers.description: Language servers for languages Duet has none for (Angular's templates): a Node script of a tool the recipe requires.

name.description: Its name in the preferences and the messages.

script.description: The script run with Node, in the tool's folder.

arguments.description: Its arguments; {{home}} stands for the tool's folder, {{project}} for the project's.

triggerCharacters.description: The characters after which it completes.

serverOptions.description: What the recipe adds to the options of a server Duet knows, by its name ("typescript-language-server"): objects merged key by key, anything else replaced. {{project}} in their texts stands for the project's folder.

requirement.description: A tool the recipe requires, and where its files go in the project's environment. {{home}} in "path" and "variables" stands for the tool's folder.

tool.description: The tool's id: one Duet knows how to install ("jdk", "node", "qt"), or any other with a "download" or a "program" to look for.

version.description: The version it needs; {{version}} in the download's addresses.

program.description: The program found in the PATH when the tool is already installed, e.g. "mvn".

systems.description: The systems it is required on; every system when it is not given.

download.description: Where to download it, by system and processor: "windows-x64", "linux-aarch64"..., else "windows", "linux", "macos", else "any".

path.description: Folders put first in the PATH. One that does not exist is left out, so a recipe lists the layouts of every system.

variables.description: Variables of the project's environment, e.g. {"JAVA_HOME": "{{home}}"}.

download.description: An archive of the tool and how to check it, or npm packages. An archive without a checksum or a known format is not installed.

npm.description: Packages installed with npm in the tool's folder instead of an archive; {{version}} stands for the requirement's version.

url.description: The archive's address; {{version}} stands for the requirement's version.

checksumUrl.description: The address of a file holding the archive's hash; {{url}} stands for the archive's address, {{version}} for the requirement's version.

algorithm.description: The hash's algorithm; "sha256" when it is not given.

format.description: The archive's format; read from the URL when it is not given.

check.description: A file of the archive that must be there once it is extracted, e.g. "bin/mvn".
